subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should OpenClaw add Discord channel/account-level granular message gates for send/read/edit/delete, or make the existing generic message-action allowlist the supported control for destructive Discord message actions?
rationale: Both paths are technically viable, but the choice changes public config shape, per-account inheritance, generated metadata, docs, and least-privilege semantics for destructive Discord message actions.

options.title: Add Discord Granular Gates
options.body: Implement a backward-compatible Discord `actions` contract that distinguishes send/read/edit/delete while preserving the current boolean shorthand.

options.title: Document Generic Allowlist Only
options.body: Keep the Discord gate coarse and make `tools.message.actions.allow` the supported way to remove destructive message actions from selected agents or the whole runtime.

options.title: Defer For Cross-Channel Design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers choose a broader cross-channel action-gate model instead of adding a Discord-specific shape now.

recommendation.title: Add Discord Granular Gates
recommendation.body: Implement a backward-compatible Discord `actions` contract that distinguishes send/read/edit/delete while preserving the current boolean shorthand.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review context and config/security history make this the best available owner for the public contract choice.
